name: United States

areaKm2.note: Contiguous United States ~7.84M km2 (B&H Table 1: 7.8M); the world_1914 United States polygon (incl. Alaska) computes to ~9.25M km2 (high).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1917 = 103,268k (high); OWID/HYDE 1917 = 99.55M (low); US Census Bureau estimate for 1917 ~103M (mid). Continental United States; territories (Philippines, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, 9.8M per B&H Table 1) excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share USA 1910 = 45.6%, 1920 = 51.2%; interpolated 1917 ~0.49. Low = COW upop/tpop 1917 = 25,310/103,268 = 0.25 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Coffman, The War to End All Wars ch. 1: on 1 April 1917 the Regular Army had ~127,500-133,000 men and ~80,000 National Guardsmen were in federal service; Navy ~65,000-69,000 and Marine Corps ~13,700. COW milper 1917 = 644k is a wartime annual average. Snapshot date: 6 April 1917 (declaration of war).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. National Guard not in federal service (total Guard ~180,000) plus Naval Militia and reserves; draft (Selective Service Act, 18 May 1917) registered 24M men later.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Navy (~69,000), Coast Artillery Corps (~20,000), field artillery, engineers, Signal Corps (incl. the Aviation Section), quartermaster and medical troops.

mobilizationRatio.note: Cited page: 4,355,000 mobilised (US War Dept 1924) by November 1918 = 0.042 of the population (low, war ended early); high 0.12 from the 1941-45 mobilisation of ~16M of ~132M (WWII production article). Mid is the potential with a longer war.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. Regular infantry regiments (~1,000-1,500 men each in April 1917) and federalised Guard infantry; Marines (~13,700) included.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M1903 Springfield excellent, very few MGs (Lewis/Benet-Mercie)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: small regular army with Mexican border experience; Guard part-time

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. 17 regular cavalry regiments (Punitive Expedition 1916) plus Guard cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: rifle-armed mounted infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regulars with Mexican campaign experience

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Coffman, The War to End All Wars (isbn:0-8131-0955-8), not read from a fetched source. ~900 field guns and howitzers (3-inch M1902, 4.7-inch, 6-inch howitzers) in April 1917; the AEF later used French 75s and 155s. Coast-defence guns excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 3-inch gun adequate, no heavy field artillery in quantity

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: no indirect-fire experience at scale

count.note: Educated guess. Qualitative statement read from the Aviation in WWI page; counts recalled from Coffman, not read from a fetched source. Cited page: US air services were far behind in 1917 and almost totally dependent on French and British combat aircraft. The Aviation Section had ~55 serviceable aircraft and fewer than 250 machines including trainers (Coffman ch. 8). Trainers and observation types; no combat aircraft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25 (a generation behind). Evidence: Curtiss JN-4 trainers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: ~130 officers in aviation

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Conway's 1906-1921: 14 dreadnoughts (South Carolina to Pennsylvania class), ~22 pre-dreadnoughts, ~10 armoured and ~20 protected/scout cruisers = 60/68/75; plus ~51 destroyers in commission = 45/51/56 (the flush-deck programme added ~270 from 1918). Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.75/0.8/0.85 (68) and destroyers 0.65/0.7/0.75 (51), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.75-1.0 and 0.75. Evidence: Nevada and Pennsylvania classes with all-or-nothing armour, 14-in guns; modern oil-fired destroyers

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers (68) and destroyers (51), both 0.65/0.7/0.75, role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional navy, little war experience; Queenstown destroyer escort force from May 1917

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. ~44 submarines, mostly coastal (Conway's).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: unreliable coastal boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: limited operations

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: Leavenworth-trained staff officers but no corps or army staffs in April 1917; Pershing built the AEF staff from scratch

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: small regular army with unit identity; Guard regiments state-based

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (motivated). Evidence: Zimmermann telegram and unrestricted U-boat war; volunteer and draft enthusiasm

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: M1903 Springfield, M1917 Browning designs coming; few MGs and guns in April 1917

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: M1917 helmet (Brodie copy) and Renault-licence tanks only from 1918

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts). Evidence: Nevada/Pennsylvania dreadnoughts with oil firing and all-or-nothing armour

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts). Evidence: Endicott-Taft coastal fortifications, Panama Canal defences

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: the world's largest rail and motor-vehicle industry; AEF supply crossed the Atlantic

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: national telephone network (AT&T), naval radio

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance. Evidence: little military aviation in April 1917

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914. Evidence: no combat aircraft in service in April 1917; Liberty engine from 1918

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: B&H Table 5 is total government spending, not military: 1.5% of GDP in 1916, 3.2% in 1917, 16.6% in 1918. The military share in 1917 is below the total: 3.2% (high, upper bound) minus the 1916 civil spending (at most 1.5%) gives at least ~1.7%; mid ~2%. Low ~0.6% = 1916 military (well under 1%, judgement). audit 2026-10-30: was 0.006/0.03/0.166 graded B, which read total government spending as the military share; mid now the military share, grade C.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Manufacturing, mining and construction ~30-35% of national income in 1917.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Herrendorf et al. via OWID: United States agriculture share of employment 1910 = 31.4%, 1920 = 25.9%; linear interpolation to 1917 = ~27.5%. 1 - 0.275 = 0.72 (mid). Large net food exporter.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching 21 per year (the 1917-18 drafts registered ~1M new 21-year-olds each June).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. US industry built almost no fighters in 1917-18 (a few SE-5 copies); AEF pursuit squadrons used SPAD and Nieuport machines.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. DH-4 observation/day bombers (~4,800 built 1918) and other service types per year; ~14,000 aircraft incl. trainers built by November 1918.

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year in 1918; US artillery production only reached volume at the Armistice.

armor.note: Educated guess. M1917 (Renault FT licence): only a few delivered by November 1918, ~950 by 1919.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Battleships and destroyers per year: battleships completed 1917-1921 (Mississippi, New Mexico, Idaho, Tennessee...) = 1/3/6; destroyers commissioned 1918-1919 (Wickes and Clemson flush-deckers) = 20/60/120. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Submarines per year 1917-1919.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Surfaced roads (~257,000 miles surfaced out of ~2.4M miles of rural roads around 1914).

railKm.note: CHAT railline United States: 1916 = 410,399 km, 1917 = 409,397 km.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Hampton Roads, Charleston, New Orleans, Galveston, San Francisco, Seattle, San Diego, Puget Sound navy yard.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914: United States 2,998,457 GRT of sea-going ships (Great Lakes excluded) (low). By April 1917 ~0.6M GRT of seized German ships and wartime building raised this to ~4M GRT (mid); high adds ~2.5M GRT of Great Lakes steamers. Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Motorised supply in France was rail-fed; Punitive Expedition of 1916 operated ~600 km into Mexico with lorries.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~21.5M horses and ~4.7M mules on US farms in 1917 (USDA figures as commonly cited).

chokepoints: Hampton Roads and New York harbour

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: oceans, coastal fortifications and population support; no invader could reach the homeland in 1917.

notes: Snapshot date 6 April 1917 (declaration of war on Germany), when the US was formally at war but not yet mobilised: forces are the peacetime-sized Regular Army, federalised Guard, Navy and Marines. The AEF grew to ~2M in France by November 1918 (World War I casualties page: 4,355,000 mobilised in total). Continental United States; territories excluded, includes empty. Aircraft in aircraft_strike (no fighters or combat types). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries). Book figures (Coffman, Conway's) not fetched online, graded at most B.
